name: Godrej Consumer Products Ltd
title: Godrej Consumer Products Ltd - 532424 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GCPL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth; EBITDA up 10% at 21.7% margin, with a revenue-presentation change.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 10% with a 21.7% margin, and reported PAT grew 10%. India standalone was the standout: 8% volume growth, 10% sales growth, 18% EBITDA growth and a 24.7% margin, led by Home Care (+12%). Africa/US/Middle East grew 20% in sales but EBITDA rose only 2% after doubling media spend, and Indonesia grew 3% in sales with 4% volume growth. From this quarter, customer-related trade spends are netted off revenue following an ICAI Expert Advisory Committee opinion, with no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT. Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

financial_highlights.change: Strong in household insecticide, air fresheners, fabric care
Personal Wash gained share; soaps muted
4% underlying volume growth; pricing pressure bottomed out

financial_highlights.metric: Africa, USA and Middle East sales growth
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +2%, media spend doubled on FMCG categories

financial_highlights.metric: Latin America and others sales growth

financial_highlights.change: About INR450 crore on NSV basis; broke even in Q4

segments.name: India Home Care
segments.commentary: Grew 12% in value with broad-based strength across household insecticides, air fresheners and fabric care; management says HI volatility is less of a concern after RNF molecule adoption.

segments.name: India Personal Care
segments.commentary: Grew 3% with soaps muted by weak category volumes and a grammage cut history; hair colour had a seasonally soft quarter and Perfume & Deodorants grew strongly double digit, led by perfumes (KS99 now pan-India).

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Sales grew 3% on 4% volume growth; management expects mid-single-digit volume and high-single-digit value growth going forward, with FY27 conditions improving.

segments.name: Africa, USA and Middle East
segments.commentary: Sales grew 20%, but EBITDA grew only 2% due to doubled media spend behind FMCG categories; management targets double-digit revenue and profit growth medium term.

segments.name: Latin America and others
segments.commentary: Sales grew 26%, EBITDA affected by one-time costs that management expects to normalise over coming quarters.

segments.name: Godrej Fab (hair/laundry/other)
segments.commentary: Annual revenue run-rate reached about INR500 crore GSV in Q4 and the business broke even in Q4, with laundry expected to be hit in Q1 by crude-linked costs.

guidance_outlook: Q1 and probably Q2 FY27 India EBITDA margins expected below normative levels (about 21.5%), though absolute EBITDA may hold up through higher revenue from pricing.
Raw material inflation cited at 7-9% on a blended basis, based on Brent around USD100-105 and palm oil around MYR4,500.
Price increases taken in April 2026: soaps about 5%, detergents 6-7%, household insecticides 4-5%; management expects to recover most of the cost inflation.
Full-year FY27 volumes may be slightly lower than planned, revenue growth slightly higher, and EBITDA slightly lower than earlier expectations at current costs.
Indonesia margins expected to improve from FY27 as pricing pressure abates; ETR for FY27 expected to be similar to FY26.
Detailed FY27 guidance and portfolio updates deferred to the analyst investor meet on 11 May 2026.
capex_capacity: Pet food: state-of-the-art plant set up in Nasik; initial volumes shipped from there.
Air fresheners: high growth globally, mainly produced in India and exported; the company will begin capturing it in reported numbers from next quarter.
Management did not give specific capex amounts or capacity utilisation figures in the call.
demand_pricing: India soaps: volumes muted; management attributes this partly to a cooler prior-year summer, a shift to liquid cleansing, and grammage cuts on small packs that are still 15-20% below last year.
Pricing: management said pricing growth is running above its earlier expectation, and soap prices are expected to rise after GST-linked cuts were passed to consumers.
Competition: in detergents GCPL is not the market leader and will follow the leader's pricing; in soaps it is gaining share but category growth is muted.
West Asia conflict is lifting middle-distillate prices (LAB, kerosene), which is a cost headwind for detergents but a competitive positive, since local players are short of feedstock.
Weather: a potential El Nino could weaken Q1 FY27 HI and soap demand, though management expects a better Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care weaker and what is the soaps outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soap markets are muted after GST and a warm/cold weather swing, that Personal Wash gained share, and that pricing will return to soaps, with Personal Care expected to grow faster in FY27 but structurally slower than Home Care.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 21.5% normative margin for India at risk given inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower margins for this quarter and next (about 3-4 months of pressure) because crude costs hit all categories, but it expects EBITDA to recover as pricing and share gains come through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the trade-spend netting on revenue and A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue and the matching other-expense lines fall by the same amount, with no change to EBITDA, PAT or cash flow; A&P looks lower on the new basis but is broadly flat year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Fab ARR and path to profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Fab's run-rate is about INR500 crore GSV (about INR450 crore NSV) and it broke even in Q4; the business is now national, with North and Maharashtra growing faster than the South.

qa_highlights.question: How does palm oil inflation compare with the FY22 cycle, and how much pricing is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is up about 10-11% (MYR4,000 to 4,500) versus 20-25% in FY22; management said the broader crude-led inflation is spread across categories, making it easier to price than a palm-oil-only spike.

qa_highlights.question: Is the household insecticide problem behind GCPL after RNF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RNF has worked in most places, HI is shifting from a zero-to-low single-digit category to a high single-digit strategy, and the seasonality issue is improving.

risks_watch: Crude and palm oil input costs (7-9% blended inflation) could widen margin pressure beyond the expected 3-4 month window.
Soap volumes remain weak; management is waiting to see whether shifts to liquid cleansing and grammage cuts persist.
Africa EBITDA was up only 2% after media spend doubled, and Latin America costs are expected to normalise.
Weather risk: El Nino may hurt Q1 FY27 HI and soaps demand, while a hot summer could help beverage/ice cream-related categories.
Presentation change: revenue is now net of trade spends, so growth comparisons with prior periods depend on the restated figures issued with the results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and Home Care, but openly cautious on near-term margins, which management expects to be below normative for one to two quarters. Management was evasive on soap competitor formulation and deferred several questions (Muuchstac, Raymond, pet food details, and specific guidance) to the 11 May investor meet.
key_quotes: In Q4, at a consolidated level, revenues grew 11% in INR terms on the back of 6% underlying volume growth.
There is no impact whatsoever on absolute EBITDA, PAT, profit after tax, total liquidity, or cash flow.
So, it may take 3 to 4 months again, of a little bit of a dip in percentage margins.
So maybe volumes will be a little lower than what we wanted at the beginning of the year, maybe revenue growth would be a little higher than what we thought we'd get at the beginning of the year.

adds.what: Pet food plant in Nasik (state-of-the-art; initial volumes shipped)

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management says FY27 revenue growth slightly higher than planned but volumes slightly lower and EBITDA slightly lower, with India margins below the ~21.5% normative in Q1 and likely Q2 due to 7-9% input inflation, offset by April price hikes (soaps ~5%, detergents 6-7%, insecticides 4-5%); detailed guidance deferred to 11 May investor meet.
